newsitem.title: USA: Key Energy sets well service acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Key Energy sets well service acquisitions.

text.p: Key Energy Group Inc said Wednesday it has acquired the assets of Edco Equipment Inc for $410,000 in cash and purchased wireline equipment and related assets from an undisclosed seller for $595,000 in cash.

The company also said it has closed on the previously announced acquisition of Shreve's Well Service Inc for $550,000 in cash and has signed a letter of intent to acquire Phoenix Well Service Inc for $2,300,000 in cash.
In addition, Key Energy said, it terminated the previously announced acquisition of Clowser Well Service for $600,000.
The net effect of these acquisitions will be an increase in Key Energy's total domestic well service rig count to 505 and its domestic well service trucking fleet to over 400 trucks.
Based on the latest publicly available information, management believes the company will be the second largest domestic well servicing contractor, Key Energy said.

Edco's assets consist of several trucks and related excavation equipment. The wireline assets consist of 10 wireline units and related equipment. Shreve's, based in Spencer, W. Va., owns five well service rigs and related equipment.
The assets acquired in these three acquisitions will be operated by Key Energy's WellTech Eastern Division, it said.

Phoenix, based in Midland, Texas, operates 11 well service rigs and three pump trucks in the Permian Basin of West Texas. Upon completion of the acquisition, which is subject to satisfactory completion of Key Energy's due diligence review, Phoenix will be operated by Key Energy's Yale E. Key Division.
"The Phoenix acquisition in particular should provide an opportunity for cost savings and synergies with our existing Yale E. Key operations," it said.
